results.summary_before: Nicolas' first Wokwi design is a simple combinational circuit that displays a lowercase letter n when the correct inputs are driven high. The design is built from basic logic gates and is intended as a first introduction to the Wokwi and Tiny Tapeout workflow. It is tested by setting inputs IN0, IN1, IN3, IN5, and IN7 on with all others off. No external hardware beyond the simulator is required, and the project has essentially no documentation beyond the pin names.

results.summary_before: This design is a three-mode clock and timer that shows a clock, a date, or a Pomodoro countdown on an external MAX7219 8-digit 7-segment display driven over SPI. Four breadboard buttons enter and leave setup mode, cycle modes and fields, increment or decrement values, and start, pause or reset the Pomodoro. Eight LED outputs report the display mode, setup state, work and break phases, alarm, and selected field. It needs the MAX7219 display and buttons as external hardware, and the documentation is brief but consistent with the pin names.

results.summary_before: DemoSiine is a demoscene-style audio-visual project that generates a 640x480 VGA video signal and a looping ~28 second audio track. The video output includes dynamic wavy sine layers and a rainbowy overlay, with user controls to enable/disable layers, pause the animation, and toggle styles. The audio engine drives a frequency synthesizer to produce the soundtrack. It requires external hardware: a TinyVGA PMOD for video output, a TT Audio PMOD for audio output, and switches for input control.

results.summary_before: This design drives an HD44780-compatible character LCD to display a clock, using a 4-bit LCD interface with data pins D4-D7 plus enable and register-select lines. Hour and minute set inputs allow the time to be adjusted, and the design runs from the Tiny Tapeout clock. The documentation consists only of links to an external GitHub README, so the internal implementation and exact test procedure are not described in the provided text. External hardware required is an HD44780 LCD module.
